findings.problem: Measured at 1440x960 and 1280x900 on owner-editing. Press −7. The reversibility bar's rect is x202 y83–152; the panel it is supposed to be inside is at y423–959. The bar is absolutely positioned at top/left/right 16px, and at 1280 and up the base position:fixed is overridden to position:static by .b-editHost .b-edit, so its containing block falls through to .b-stick, which is position:sticky (b.css:947). The result, screenshotted: an opaque ink block with a hairline under it, reading "Send the invitations moved 7 days earlier. Undo Ctrl Z", painted across MARA & FINN and straight through the middle of the 148px count — the count rect is y106–233, they overlap, and elementFromPoint over the numerals returns .b-undoText, so it takes the pointer there too. The panel below keeps its 78px band empty for a bar that never arrives. The comment at b.css:632-634 states the reason no position is declared — "the base rule is already position: fixed, which is a positioned ancestor for the bar below" — and that is exactly the assumption the 1280 rule breaks, so the code and its comment disagree at the two widths every desk frame is shot at. The gate runs this case at 1280 and 1440 (interaction-check.mjs:889-905) and passes, because inView (top >= 0, bottom <= innerHeight) and reachable (elementFromPoint) are both true of a bar sitting on the horizon. The named decision — one node that travels into the top of the editor while it is open — is asserted nowhere.
findings.fix: Add position: relative; to .b-editHost .b-edit in the min-width:1280 block (b.css:949-955). Verified in the browser: the bar moves to y428 inside the panel whose top is y411, and the 78px reserve is what holds it. Then replace the two placement assertions at interaction-check.mjs:903-904 with the property the decision owes: with a panel open, const u = document.querySelector('.b-undo').getBoundingClientRect(), e = document.querySelector('.b-edit').getBoundingClientRect(); assert u.top >= e.top - 1 && u.bottom <= e.bottom + 1; and after Escape, assert the bar's rect does not intersect .b-horizon's rect, at all four widths.

findings.element: [data-past="listed"] rules at b.css:381-383, states.print (render-b.js:1015-1031), and the assertion at interaction-check.mjs:1134-1139
findings.problem: Measured, not inferred. Open ?v=record&state=phone, &state=desk and &state=print: .b-behindSummary computes display:none, details.open is false, and 0 of 3 .b-behindRow pass checkVisibility({contentVisibilityAuto:true}). Chromium hides a closed <details>'s content through ::details-content { content-visibility: hidden }, which display:block on a descendant cannot override — so b.css:382-383 are dead rules and b.css:381 deletes the only control that could have opened it. In The long view — the room whose own copy is "Everything that happened, and today drawn on the rail" — the past is not listed in full, it is gone: We said yes, The Orchard reserved and the cancelled hotel search sit in the DOM reachable by nobody, and that room's guest surfaces drop to zero focusable elements. The shipped print state is the other half: ?state=print in the default room is past=folded, so the A4 keepsake goes to paper carrying a live cursor:pointer disclosure reading "Behind you 3 moments" with its rows absent — exactly what b.css:379-380 says must never happen. The gate has an assertion for this (1136, "the printed sheet never prints a closed control") and it passes by proving getComputedStyle(summary).display === "none" — the very thing that causes the loss — and only in the record room, so the print state that actually ships is never graded. The right instrument was already in the file thirty lines earlier (1115 uses checkVisibility).
findings.fix: Force it in the DOM, not in the cascade. In behindBlock (render-b.js:253) build the disclosure as h("details.b-behindDetails", { open: forced ? "" : null }, […]) with var forced = C.rootEl().getAttribute("data-past") === "listed" || o.print === true; and pass { print: true } from states.print (render-b.js:1025) so the sheet is open whichever room it is printed from. Keep b.css:381; delete the two dead rules at b.css:382-383. Then rewrite interaction-check.mjs:1136 to the property that matters, over both rooms: for (const v of ["approach", "record"]) open ?state=print and assert every .b-behindRow passes checkVisibility({contentVisibilityAuto:true}) and that no summary in the sheet is visible; add ?v=record&state=phone to the same loop.

findings.problem: Driven end to end. In owner-editing press Hidden: the row drops to --fore-62 with a dashed tick, the badge reads Hidden, the accessible name ends "Hidden from guests.", the bar says "Send the invitations is now hidden from guests." and it undoes cleanly. Press Done, then press Preview — the control sitting 300px away in the same bar. The guest artifact lists all seven moments, Send the invitations among them. Visibility is written to a DOM attribute only; ahead() reads F.live() from the fixture and Preview re-mounts from the fixture, so the field titled "What guests see" is the one field in that panel with no effect on what a guest sees. This is not a general limit of the prototype: renaming writes through to the record (setTitle, render-b.js:437) and Add pushes to F.milestones (729), so the owner has already been taught that edits carry. It is also the promise the product is sold on — a couple must be able to keep a surprise off the page — and it is disprovable in two clicks. Six assertions cover the toggle (interaction-check.mjs:522-529, 873-882) and every one of them stops at the owner's own DOM.
findings.fix: Make the record the store and the guest lists read it. In setVisibility (render-b.js:419) add recordFor(item.getAttribute("data-id")).hidden = hidden; before the attribute write. Give the two list accessors an owner flag: function ahead(clock, owner) { return F.live().filter(function (m) { return m.date && daysFrom(clock, m.date) > 0 && (owner || !m.hidden); }).sort(…); } and the same guard in behind() (render-b.js:50). Pass o.owner from measure() (129) and from behindBlock() (220). Then assert it: from owner-editing press Hidden, press [data-act="done"], press [data-act="preview"], and require the guest's .b-item count to be one fewer and document.body.innerText not to contain the hidden title — and the reverse after an undo.

findings.element: backdropOf (audit.mjs:80-91) and the tracking check (audit.mjs:184-199, 287-294); live victims .tl-caption (shell.css:207-213) and .b-previewStrip (b.css:479-489)
findings.problem: Two proofs, both run. (a) backdropOf walks backgroundColor only. This lab paints its page ground ONLY as a background-image — background-color: var(--paper) plus linear-gradient(var(--page-wash)…), a decision documented twice at shell.css:114-121 and 140-147 — so for everything outside .b-field the gate measures against white while the pixels are #111. .tl-caption is --ink-62, is scored 5.34:1 and passes in all eleven states; screenshotted at 1440 in the default room its band is solid black with nothing in it, 1.05:1, while shell.css:206 says it is set "as quietly as it can be and still pass AA". The same blind spot hides a real control: press Preview from owner-flight and .b-previewStrip paints "Preview" and "Back to the plan" in literal var(--ink) (b.css:488-489) on that same #111 page. Screenshotted: an empty black band 1180px wide. The owner's only way out of the preview is invisible, its border with it; the behaviour gate clicks it and reports "the way back works" (interaction-check.mjs:1054-1062) without asking whether it can be seen, and audit.mjs presses nothing, so the strip exists in no audited page. (b) The tracking check compares each family+size to itself within one state and never to the six declared --track-* steps, which is not the check round 1 asked for. Proof: set .b-dayDate to letter-spacing: 0.077em, rebuild, run audit.mjs --states=day — tracking pass, 0 to fix, a seventh undeclared value ships clean. And because tracks is rebuilt inside each per-state evaluate, the defect it was written for — the same 20px string tracked two ways on two surfaces, .b-when and .b-dayDate, which live in different states — is invisible by construction.
findings.fix: (a) In backdropOf (audit.mjs:83), before the alpha test, composite the wash: const cs = getComputedStyle(node); const img = (cs.backgroundImage.match(/rgba?\([^)]+\)/g) || []).pop(); let bg = parse(cs.backgroundColor); if (img) { const g = parse(img); bg = bg && bg.a > 0 ? over(g, bg) : g; } — then continue with the existing stack logic, so a gradient ground counts as ground. Re-run the gate, then paint the strip from the ladder rather than from literals: b.css:488-489 become .b-previewStrip { border-bottom-color: var(--fore-16); } .b-previewStrip .b-where { color: var(--fore-62); } .b-previewStrip .b-act { color: var(--fore); border-color: var(--fore-16); }. (b) Read the six --track-* values off getComputedStyle(document.documentElement) inside the audit script, convert each to px at the element's own font-size, and push a tracking entry whenever a non-furniture element's computed letterSpacing is not within 0.02px of one of them; hoist tracks out of AUDIT into the outer report so one family+size carrying two values across two states fails as well.

findings.element: place() (render-b.js:153-207), which sorts a copy of the rows and writes style.top only, against .b-measure role="list" aria-label="What is still ahead, nearest first" (render-b.js:136-137)
findings.problem: Driven at 1440 from owner-editing: three presses of +7. The rows now read, in the DOM and therefore in the accessibility tree and in tab order, 16, 44, 37, 44, 51, 65, 79. The tab sweep confirms it — "Open Send the invitations. Saturday 29 August" is reached before "Open Final dress fitting. Saturday 22 August", while on screen the fitting sits 126px above the invitations. place() sorts, uses the sort to assign tops, and throws it away; nothing ever reorders the nodes. So the one claim the list's own accessible name makes stops being true the moment the owner uses the product's primary gesture, and a keyboard or screen-reader owner works down a column whose order no longer matches the column a sighted owner is looking at. Undo of a delete has the same shape (render-b.js:710: insert before the recorded neighbour, or append at the end when that neighbour is gone). Nothing in the 357 assertions reads DOM order — "the nearest item is still the one marked" (376) checks the painted lead mark only. I proved the gate is indifferent: with the fix below applied the suite still reports 357 assertions, 0 failing, exactly as without it.
findings.fix: Put the DOM in the order the sort already computed, without losing the animation. In place(), immediately after items.sort() (render-b.js:161) insert: var dom = Array.prototype.slice.call(measureEl.querySelectorAll('.b-item')); if (items.some(function (el, i) { return dom[i] !== el; })) { items.forEach(function (el) { el.style.top = el.offsetTop + 'px'; measureEl.appendChild(el); }); void measureEl.offsetHeight; } — pinning each row to where it already is and flushing layout before the loop below writes the new tops means the re-inserted nodes still transition. Verified in the browser: mid-flight computed top 520.685px against a target of 540px, so the move still animates; DOM order after +21 is 16,37,44,44,51,65,79; focus stays on the stepper; the gate stays at 357/0. Then assert it: after three +7 presses, Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.b-item')).map(function (el) { return +el.getAttribute('data-away'); }) must equal its own sorted copy, and again after undoing a delete.

biggestWin: The owner's fifteen seconds are finished and they are proven. Everything round 2 called a promise is real and reversible now: Add builds a row and focuses an empty field, the title field writes through to the row and to its accessible name, delete keeps the live node and puts it back where it was with focus on it, a typed date is parsed and refused with a reason when it has gone or overshoots the day, and one history stack carries a closure per entry so Ctrl Z and the bar reverse the same thing. Driven twenty presses into the ceiling, the count, the date line, the row's name, the readout, the gap sentence and the lead mark all move in the same frame, the steppers hold still under the pointer, and the page keeps its scroll and its focus. 357 assertions and a clean measured gate stand behind it. What is left is not that work — it is the handoff and the rooms around it, and it is one focused day. Two of my five findings exist only for the person the product is for: press Hidden and the guest still sees it, and open the record room or the printed keepsake and the past is not listed in full, it is missing altogether. Two more are visible in the first frame a founder would demo: at 1440 the reversibility bar paints across the 148px count, and the only way back from Preview is black on black. The fifth is the reading order quietly ceasing to be what the list calls itself. None of them is a different decision and none is a rebuild — four are single-rule fixes and one is a twenty-line accessor change. What should worry the founder more than any of them is that all five passed both gates: two assertions written to guard this exact ground pass by proving the wrong property, and the contrast gate cannot see the ground the whole lab stands on. Fix the five, close the two gate holes, and this is at the bar.
